title: Paris 1606 Cistercian strict Canon: independent complete original-image collation
reviewer: Independent AI source review panel (1606 recovery, disjoint complete-image collation and separate extent review)
scope: Complete strict Eucharistic Canon constituent of the Paris 1606 Cistercian missal: from the printed CANON MISSÆ. heading and Te igitur on printed p.190, BSB canvas244/full-provider-PDF 245, through Per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum. Amen. on printed p.197 left, canvas251/PDF252, immediately before Orémus/Præcéptis/Pater noster. All five printed seasonal Communicantes insertions and the Pascha/Pentecost Hanc igitur insertion, their rubrics, continuation signs, name cues and 26 crosses are included in source order. The fourth page in this sequence is BSB-labelled193 but actually misprinted 192. The later Ordinary under the same Canon Missæ running head is explicitly outside this strict Canon. Whole-book and complete-Ordinary coverage remain partial; this constituent is independent of the unchanged accepted offertory and inherits no wording from another edition.
method: The recovered prior-author draft was not accepted from its manifests. Distinct source reviewers directly opened all eight original embedded JPEG page images and collated every included word, rubric, abbreviation, accent, punctuation mark, cross, asterisk, name placeholder, variant ending and source block against the prior transcript. Disjoint review covered printed190–191 (units1–14 plus the visible unit15 prefix), printed192–sequence193 (unit15 suffix plus units16–22), and printed194–197 (units23–35). The split Mat-/thæi name and every other page/column join were reconciled. A separate reviewer directly inspected all eight images and adjacent whole-PDF pages to verify the independent complete-extent census, all five seasonal Communicantes forms, the Pascha/Pentecost Hanc insertion, all six rubrics, all26 printed crosses and all35 units. Eleven source-supported reading corrections across seven units and preservation of three printed Communicantes paragraphs were reconciled in a new version while prior proposals and review findings remained intact. Each page reviewer then accepted its exact corrected v3 bodies and selected-line hashes; the extent reviewer separately accepted v3 page/unit incidence and serialization. Finally the coordinator verified exact manifest strings, payload bytes, edition/derivation/rights identities, every selected-line hash and all binding/census pins. The existing prior extent-freeze is corroborating history; no assertion that the recovered reviewers made a blind pre-transcription freeze depends on that earlier file. No OCR, other-edition wording or familiar Roman formula controls this acceptance.
normalization_limit: Direct source reading of original BSB 1606 scans: long s becomes s; split display initials merge in sentence case; source line wraps and line-end word divisions join inside semantic blocks. Printed nasal suspension bars, the standard -us brevigraph, -q;/-que suspension and Dñi contraction are expanded without adding absent accents. The marked vir- contraction in the Nativity insertion is expanded as unaccented virginis; no acute is inferred from the separately printed main Communicantes form. Printed u/v, j, æ/œ, actual accents, case within sentences, punctuation, parentheses, ampersands, N. placeholders and abbreviated rubric/variant endings remain. Red crosses are serialized as ✠, including crosses inside words; printed asterisks remain *. Rubrics are separate units. Communicantes opening and continuation remain separate around the five proper insertions, preserving column/source order. The source’s duplicated & & in Supplices and Easter diem sacratíssimam are retained. No familiar Roman wording or missing ending is supplied. The 35 UTF-8 NFC semantic units retain source order. The main Communicantes continuation preserves three source paragraphs, separated by a blank LF line; its selected physical-line range includes those two blank lines. Other units occupy one physical line. The complete artifact ends with LF; each unit selection hash excludes its terminating LF. Running heads after the opening title, page numbers, catchwords, ornament, type colour, line/column geometry and chant notes are recorded as facsimile/paratext rather than text; all sung words within the Canon, including its final Amen, remain. This is a normalized reading transcription, not a glyph-diplomatic or musical edition.
